image_description: A close-up view of a bicycle disc brake assembly mounted on a spoked wheel. The image features a metallic, drilled rotor (disc) with ventilation holes, a black caliper housing with visible branding/logos, and red adjustment knobs. The background consists of blurred wheel spokes against a neutral grey backdrop.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Circular metal rotor (disc), notably larger in diameter than its thickness.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor is clearly circular and thin relative to its diameter, consistent with a disc brake profile.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caliper is cast metal mounted over rotor edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A black caliper assembly is visibly straddling the outer edge of the rotor.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rotor is mounted to wheel hub with visible lug bolt pattern.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The center hub area where the rotor mounts to the axle is occluded by the caliper body and fork/frame structure; no lug bolts are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rotor is ventilated (two plates with cooling fins) or solid.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor exhibits a pattern of cross-drilled holes, which serves as ventilation/cooling, matching the 'ventilated' description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Brake pads are rectangular friction material blocks pressing against rotor faces.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The brake pads are internal components housed within the caliper jaws and are not directly visible from this exterior angle.
A black hose/cable entry point is visible at the bottom of the caliper assembly, consistent with hydraulic line connection.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface shows machined concentric grooves or cross-drilled holes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor surface clearly displays a pattern of circular cross-drilled holes.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface exhibits heat discoloration (blue/brown tint) from use.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor appears uniformly silver/metallic without significant blueing or browning indicative of heavy heat cycling.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caliper is cast aluminum or iron.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The caliper has the smooth, slightly textured finish typical of cast metal alloys used in bicycle components.

artifact_observations.location: Green square logo on caliper body
artifact_observations.reasoning: The green square contains white characters that resemble text but are nonsensical/garbled, a common AI artifact when rendering logos or labels.
Several spokes appear to merge into the background or the caliper body without clear attachment points, suggesting slight geometric inconsistency.
The drilled holes lack distinct depth shadows, appearing somewhat flat or painted on rather than physically punched through the metal.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the object is correctly classified as a disk brake and not a generic mechanical part.
To analyze the garbled text in the green square and determine if it's a hallucination or a stylized brand mark.
To verify the physical connectivity of the spokes to the hub and ensure the rotor is a continuous ring without breaks.
To assess the realism of the metal reflections and the depth of field blur.

focus_areas: Legibility and structure of the text/logo on the caliper
Depth and realism of the drilled holes in the rotor
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'text_gibberish' artifact. In industrial photography, logos are crisp. If the OCR expert finds no valid characters, this is a strong indicator of AI generation. Also, check if the 'flatness' of the drilled holes is confirmed by the depth auditor.
